units.en: Navy intel is generally focused on a country's navy, and having too little navy intel over an enemy can make finding and contesting their navy harder. It can range between ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧.⟦2⟧
The main sources for navy intel are the target country's ⟦0⟧, its ⟦1⟧'s ⟦2⟧, and ⟦3⟧ with the target country's ⟦4⟧. Intel gained from the first two is as follows:

Fighting enemy ⟦0⟧ in ⟦1⟧ can temporarily provide navy intel over the ships' owning countries. The maximum effective cap on navy intel gained in this way is ⟦2⟧,⟦3⟧ and the maximum hard cap on navy intel gained in this way is ⟦4⟧.⟦5⟧ The hard cap does not contribute directly to a country's navy intel, but intel gained within it can act as a buffer that absorbs intel decay before it can affect a country's effective navy intel.

The base daily navy intel gain rate is ⟦0⟧ per ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧ per enemy ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧ per enemy ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧ per enemy ⟦7⟧, ⟦8⟧ per enemy ⟦9⟧, and ⟦10⟧ per aircraft hosted on ⟦11⟧ in the naval battle(s). The actual amount of intel gained from ⟦12⟧ per day is (for all intel types):⟦13⟧

Certain ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ can reduce the amount of navy intel given to other countries or increase the amount of navy intel gained from other countries. Notably, the ⟦2⟧ spirit for ⟦3⟧ and the ⟦4⟧ decision for the ⟦5⟧ unlocked by ⟦6⟧ can lower the amount of navy intel given to other countries significantly. With ⟦7⟧, the ⟦8⟧ ⟦9⟧ spirit also reduces the amount of navy intel given to other countries.
⟦0⟧ can provide navy intel based on their levels and overall coverage. See the dedicated ⟦1⟧ section for more details.

⟦0⟧ unlocks many more potential sources for navy intel, both from ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧. See the dedicated ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧ sections for more details. Without ⟦5⟧, countries can receive additional navy intel based on their decryption level relative to target countries' encryption levels. See the dedicated ⟦6⟧ section for more details.

Finally, when in a ⟦0⟧ with an ally who has more navy intel on a target country, the observing country receives ⟦1⟧⟦2⟧ of the difference between them and their ally as bonus navy intel against the target country.

Having too little navy intel against a target country applies a penalty when attempting to establish or contest ⟦0⟧ against the target country's ⟦1⟧. Below ⟦2⟧ navy intel against a target country, the observer country receives a ⟦3⟧ penalty to their ⟦4⟧ against the target country for each percentage point of naval intel missing, down to a maximum penalty of ⟦5⟧⟦6⟧ at ⟦7⟧ or lower naval intel.

If an observer country has more navy intel over a target country than the target has over the observer, the observer gains a bonus to their spotting speed against the target and the target gains a penalty to their spotting speed against the observer. Starting with a navy intel difference of at least ⟦0⟧ percentage points, the observer gains ⟦1⟧ spotting speed for every percentage point of difference in navy intel, up to a maximum of ⟦2⟧ spotting speed at a ⟦3⟧ percentage point difference in navy intel. The target receives a mirrored ⟦4⟧ spotting speed penalty per percentage point difference, up to a maximum penalty of ⟦5⟧.

With ⟦0⟧, the observer also takes reduced damage from the target's naval mines if they have more navy intel on the target than the target has on them. Starting with a navy intel difference of at least ⟦1⟧ percentage points, the observer receives ⟦2⟧ damage from the target's naval mines for every percentage point of difference in navy intel, up to a maximum of ⟦3⟧ damage from the target's naval mines at a ⟦4⟧ percentage point difference in navy intel.

Air intel is generally focused on a country's air force and provides bonuses to detecting aircraft, as well as early notifications for ⟦0⟧. It can range between ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧.⟦3⟧
The main sources for air intel are the target country's ⟦0⟧'s ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧ with the target country's ⟦3⟧, and ⟦4⟧ and ⟦5⟧ involving the target country's ⟦6⟧. Intel gained from ⟦7⟧ is as follows:

Fighting enemy ⟦0⟧ in ⟦1⟧ can temporarily provide navy intel over the ships' owning countries. The maximum effective cap on air intel gained in this way is ⟦2⟧,⟦3⟧ and the maximum hard cap on air intel gained in this way is ⟦4⟧.⟦5⟧ The hard cap does not contribute directly to a country's air intel, but intel gained within it can act as a buffer that absorbs intel decay before it can affect a country's effective air intel.
The base daily air intel gain rate is ⟦0⟧ per ⟦1⟧ with ⟦2⟧, plus ⟦3⟧ per enemy plane in those combats, all multiplied by ⟦4⟧.⟦5⟧ The actual amount of intel gained from ⟦6⟧ per day is:⟦7⟧

⟦0⟧ involving enemy ⟦1⟧ also generate air intel. The base daily air intel gain rate from ⟦2⟧ is ⟦3⟧ per ⟦4⟧ with at least one enemy ⟦5⟧, plus ⟦6⟧ per enemy plane in those ⟦7⟧, all multiplied by ⟦8⟧.⟦9⟧ This is further modified by a dynamic gain rate and decay rate given to all intel gained from ⟦10⟧, as well as by ⟦11⟧' reconnaissance values; see the dedicated ⟦12⟧ section for more details about these. The maximum effective cap on air intel gained in this way is ⟦13⟧,⟦14⟧ and the maximum hard cap on civilian intel gained in this way is ⟦15⟧.⟦16⟧ The hard cap does not contribute directly to a country's air intel, but intel gained within it can act as a buffer that absorbs intel decay before it can affect a country's effective air intel.

⟦0⟧ involving enemy ⟦1⟧ can also generate air intel. The base daily air intel gain rate from ⟦2⟧ is ⟦3⟧ per ⟦4⟧ with at least one enemy ⟦5⟧, plus ⟦6⟧ per enemy ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧ and ⟦9⟧ per enemy non-⟦10⟧ ⟦11⟧ in those ⟦12⟧, all multiplied by ⟦13⟧. This is further modified by a dynamic gain rate and decay rate given to all intel gained from ⟦14⟧; see the dedicated ⟦15⟧ section for more details about these. The maximum effective cap on air intel gained in this way is ⟦16⟧,⟦17⟧ and the maximum hard cap on civilian intel gained in this way is ⟦18⟧.⟦19⟧ The hard cap does not contribute directly to a country's air intel, but intel gained within it can act as a buffer that absorbs intel decay before it can affect a country's effective air intel.

Certain ⟦0⟧ and ⟦1⟧ can reduce the amount of air intel given to other countries or increase the amount of air intel gained from other countries. Notably, the ⟦2⟧ spirit for ⟦3⟧ and the ⟦4⟧ decision for the ⟦5⟧ unlocked by ⟦6⟧ can lower the amount of air intel given to other countries significantly. With ⟦7⟧, the ⟦8⟧ ⟦9⟧ spirit also reduces the amount of air intel given to other countries.
⟦0⟧ can provide particularly large amounts of air intel based on their levels and overall coverage. See the dedicated ⟦1⟧ section for more details.

⟦0⟧ unlocks many more potential sources for air intel, both from ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧. See the dedicated ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧ sections for more details. Without ⟦5⟧, countries can receive additional air intel based on their decryption level relative to target countries' encryption levels. See the dedicated ⟦6⟧ section for more details.

Finally, when in a ⟦0⟧ with an ally who has more air intel on a target country, the observing country receives ⟦1⟧⟦2⟧ of the difference between them and their ally as bonus air intel against the target country.

Air intel is closely tied to the detection of ⟦0⟧. Having at least ⟦1⟧ air intel is required to know when a raid has been launched, but having more allows for incoming raids to be detected while they are still in their preparation phases. Each percentage point of air intel against a target allows raids to be detected one percentage point earlier into their preparation phase: ⟦2⟧ air intel allows raids to be detected at ⟦3⟧ preparation, ⟦4⟧ air intel allows raids to be detected at ⟦5⟧ preparation, ⟦6⟧ air intel allows raids to be detected at ⟦7⟧ preparation, etc.⟦8⟧
It should be noted that unlike army intel, air intel does not provide any bonuses to ⟦0⟧. However, with ⟦1⟧, having decrypted enemy ciphers provides some bonuses to ⟦2⟧. See ⟦3⟧ for more details.

⟦0⟧ can provide additional intel of all types against other countries depending on their coverage. At their maximum, they can provide up to ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧, and ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧ over other countries.⟦9⟧ Intel from ⟦10⟧ is considered "static intel", meaning it is gained and lost instantaneously.

The intel gathering efficiency of ⟦0⟧ depends on both how many provinces of the target country are within their radar coverage, how many provinces the target country controls in total (the more provinces they control, the less intel is gathered from radar coverage over a single province), and the level of the ⟦1⟧ itself. At a maximum level of 6, a single ⟦2⟧ has an intel gathering efficiency of ⟦3⟧,⟦4⟧ and this decreases linearly with each missing level, down to ca. ⟦5⟧ efficiency at level 1. When multiple ⟦6⟧ cover a single province, the intel gathering efficiency of each station beyond the first is decreased by ⟦7⟧ for that province.

At full, 100% radar coverage over a country's controlled land provinces, ⟦0⟧ can provide ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧, and ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧ over that country.⟦9⟧ These are multiplied by each ⟦10⟧'s intel gathering efficiency and are also decreased linearly as the fraction of controlled land provinces with radar coverage decreases. A ⟦11⟧ can provide additional intel on other countries based on how many provinces in its coverage range are land provinces controlled by the target country. At a maximum, this constitutes ⟦12⟧ ⟦13⟧, ⟦14⟧ ⟦15⟧, ⟦16⟧ ⟦17⟧, and ⟦18⟧ ⟦19⟧ per ⟦20⟧,⟦21⟧ multiplied by that station's intel gathering efficiency and the number of land provinces it covers that are controlled by the target country, then divided by the total amount of provinces covered by the station.

Radar coverage over sea provinces also incorporates a given ⟦0⟧'s intel gathering efficiency, but works based on the number and type of ⟦1⟧ operating in the ⟦2⟧ to which the province belongs. Each ⟦3⟧ can provide up to ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧ against its owner, each ⟦6⟧ can provide up to ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧ against its owner, each ⟦9⟧ can provide up to ⟦10⟧ ⟦11⟧ against its owner, and each ⟦12⟧ can provide up to ⟦13⟧ ⟦14⟧ against its owner,⟦15⟧ all multiplied by the fraction of radar coverage over the ⟦16⟧ in which they are operating and the intel gathering efficiency of the ⟦17⟧ providing that coverage.

⟦0⟧ also provide intel depending on the fraction of a target country's ⟦1⟧ that pass through the ⟦2⟧ they cover, including those used for ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, and transporting troops. As a baseline, this is ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧, and ⟦11⟧ ⟦12⟧ per ⟦13⟧ per ⟦14⟧,⟦15⟧ multiplied by the fraction of the target's convoys that pass through that region as well as each ⟦16⟧'s intel gathering efficiency and overall coverage of each ⟦17⟧.
⟦0⟧ can provide additional sources of civilian, army, navy, and/or air intel.
⟦0⟧ at ⟦1⟧ provide a multiplicative bonus to all gathered intel. Each of the four types of intel (civilian, army, navy, and air) has its own upgrade: ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧, and ⟦5⟧.

Intel networks in a country can provide civilian, army, navy, and air intel to the networks' owners against the target country. These can be built up using ⟦0⟧ performing the ⟦1⟧ ⟦2⟧ and, once a sufficient size is reached, quieted using the ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧. The maximum amount of intel provided by a network is ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧, ⟦7⟧ ⟦8⟧, ⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧, and ⟦11⟧ ⟦12⟧,⟦13⟧ all of which are scaled by ⟦14⟧ the intel network coverage in the target country. It does not matter if the networks are active or have been quieted, their coverage contributes to providing intel regardless. This amount can also be increased with the ⟦15⟧ ⟦16⟧ upgrade. ⟦17⟧ is based on the coverage of ⟦18⟧ instead of just states, with a ⟦19⟧ states coverage multiplier if no ⟦20⟧ are covered by intel networks, though the total maximum of ⟦21⟧ ⟦22⟧ from intel networks still applies.
